✅ Airbnb Dynamic Pricing Project – EDA and Data Cleaning Summary


---

                                                1. ✅ Dataset Overview

Original Dataset contained 17 columns and 14 lakh+ rows.

Data features included room details, host details, location, pricing, availability, and reviews.

---

                                              2.✅ Data Cleaning Performed

Renamed Columns for clarity (e.g., room_id, room_price, etc.).

Split Coordinates into Latitude and Longitude columns.

Removed Duplicates based on key identifiers.

Dropped Useless Columns:

updated_date (it was outdated and irrelevant).


Handled Missing Values:

Reviews missing were filled using the mean value.

Null coordinates were carefully handled.


Filtered Price Outliers:

Removed extreme listings with room_price > 1000 USD for realistic analysis.

---

                                           3.✅ Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

3.1 Working with Sample Data

Due to the large dataset size (14 lakh+ rows),
a random sample of 5000 rows was taken for plotting graphs and performing fast analysis.

This ensured better visualization, faster performance, and avoided system crashes.

---

3.2 Price Distribution

Most Airbnb listings are priced between $50 and $250.

Long tail observed with few expensive luxury listings.


3.3 Room Type Analysis

Entire Home/Apt listings dominate the dataset (~65-70%).

Private Rooms are second most common.

Shared Rooms and Hotel Rooms are very rare.


3.4 Room Type vs Average Price

Entire Home/Apt has the highest average price.

Private Rooms and Shared Rooms are significantly cheaper.


3.5 Top 10 Cities by Listings

Cities like New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris, and Sydney have the most Airbnb listings.


3.6 Average Price by City

Major tourist cities like New York and London show relatively higher average prices.


3.7 Minimum Nights vs Price

No strong direct relation found.

Most bookings were short-term (1–7 nights) based.


3.8 Availability vs Price

Availability across 365 days doesn’t directly correlate with higher prices.


3.9 Correlation Heatmap

Number of Reviews and Reviews per Month showed strong positive correlation (0.76).

Room Price is largely independent from other numerical features like reviews, minimum nights, and availability.


3.10 Room Type Distribution Pie Chart

Visually confirmed that Entire Homes dominate the Airbnb listings.


✅ Key Insights (Row-wise)

1) Room price distribution is right-skewed — most listings are priced between $50 and $250, with a few luxury listings priced much higher.

2) Entire Home/Apt listings dominate the dataset, making up around 65-70% of all listings.

3) Private Rooms are the second most common, while Shared Rooms and Hotel Rooms are rare.

4) Entire Home/Apt listings have the highest average price compared to other room types.

5) Cities like New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris, Sydney have the highest number of Airbnb listings.

6) Average prices vary significantly across cities — cities like New York and London have higher average prices.

7) Minimum nights required for booking has no strong direct impact on room price.

8) Availability of listings (number of available days in a year) also does not directly influence room price.

9) Number of Reviews and Reviews Per Month have a strong positive correlation (0.76), meaning properties with more total reviews also have higher monthly reviews.

10) Room Price shows no strong correlation with numerical features like reviews, availability, or minimum nights, meaning price depends more on room type, city, location rather than review counts.

11) During EDA, a sampled dataset (5000 rows) was used instead of the full dataset to ensure better plotting speed and clearer graphs.
